items.title: Big Tech sues over California plan to limit kids’ scrolling
items.summary: Social media platforms Google, Meta, and TikTok say California’s law violates their free-speech rights and interferes with parents’ decisions.

items.title: Attacks on supermarket and blood storage systems prompt US warning
items.summary: US agencies have issued a warning about remote access to industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems.

items.title: Phone return scams: where a real delivery and a fake return end up in a bill for you
items.summary: Phone return scams are part of a very convincing social engineering method where the criminals get a phone and you get billed.

items.title: NIKKE PC launcher compromise put players’ passwords and personal files at risk
items.summary: Players of Goddess of Victory: NIKKE are being urged to check their PCs after attackers tampered with files used by the game’s Windows launcher.

items.title: Scammers use AI-generated images of missing pets to extort owners
items.summary: Scammers are using AI images to enhance their "I've found your missing pet and want money to return it to you" schemes.

items.title: Vizio, Samsung smart TVs seem to ignore tracking opt outs
items.summary: If you thought that opting out of surveillance on your smart TV would give you your privacy back, think again.

items.title: The fake $750 Apple Cash reward that pays out nothing
items.summary: A fake $750 Apple Cash offer uses scripted checks and fake countdowns. Affiliate marketers earn a commission; you get no reward.

items.title: mSecure tells users to change passwords but won’t say why [updated]
items.summary: mSecure has urged users to protect information stored in its app, but hasn’t explained what happened or whether anyone’s data was exposed.

items.title: Chrome 157 fixes 213 security issues, including 7 critical flaws
items.summary: Your browser may not have updated itself yet. Here’s how to check your version and install the fix manually.

items.title: A hidden backdoor put 1.3 million TV boxes to work for criminals
items.summary: Videostrong planted a backdoor in more than 1.3 million Android set-top boxes and sold criminals access to the resulting botnet.

items.title: Hackers put porn on public billboards and claim it was “far too easy”
items.summary: A hacking group called Leakers$ gained access to remote management software for billboards and used it to show porn.

items.title: Revolve card breach: 1.5 million people may be affected
items.summary: Revolve says shoppers’ saved card details were stolen. A Texas filing suggests as many as 1.5 million people may be affected.

items.title: 5 stars for sale: Inside the underground fake review trade
items.summary: Underground sellers offer five-star reviews and charge up to $1,100 to make negative feedback disappear.

items.title: Applebee’s customer data exposed by password left in app
items.summary: A researcher found an embedded password in Applebee’s app that exposed customer data.

items.title: A week in security (October 26 – November 1)
items.summary: A list of topics we covered in the week of October 26 to November 1 of 2026

items.title: Fake PDF and search tools hijacked searches for 13.4 million Chrome users
items.summary: 319 Chrome extensions sent search queries through servers controlled by their operators, allowing them to see what users searched for.

items.title: Photo ID, bank checks, face scan? The UK’s age-check options
items.summary: Ofcom has set out four possible age-verification methods for UK’s under-16 social media ban.

items.title: Binance hit by largest-ever crypto theft, with $6.3 billion stolen
items.summary: Attackers stole about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance in what analysts say is the largest crypto theft on record.

items.title: Hackers steal and publish data on 41,000 Homeland Security workers
items.summary: A hacker group claims it stole data on 41,000 DHS employees, exposing work contact details and internal group memberships.

items.title: Malicious Firefox extensions impersonate popular crypto wallets
items.summary: Fake Firefox extensions posing as Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget targeted users to steal crypto wallet recovery phrases and private keys.
